questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the following computer terms giving an example for each.

(a) Automation. (2 marks)

(b) Control system. (2 marks)

(c) Robot. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Automation (2 marks).** Automation is the use of machines, computers and control technology to carry out a task or a whole process with little or no human intervention. It saves time and labour, gives consistent quality and removes human error from repetitive work. *Example:* an automatic bottling line in a brewery in Douala, where bottles are filled, capped and labelled by machines; other examples are an ATM dispensing cash and automatic doors.

**(b) Control system (2 marks).** A control system is a combination of input devices (sensors), a processor (a microprocessor or computer) and output devices (actuators such as motors, heaters or valves) which monitors a physical quantity and automatically adjusts it to keep it at a required value, usually by using feedback (the output is measured again by the sensor and compared with the target value). *Example:* the thermostat of an air conditioner (the temperature sensor reads the room temperature, the processor compares it with the set value and switches the compressor on or off); other examples are traffic-light control and automatic irrigation.

**(c) Robot (2 marks).** A robot is a programmable, computer-controlled machine, fitted with sensors and with moving parts (arms, wheels, grippers), which can carry out physical tasks automatically, often in places that are dangerous, hot, or too repetitive for humans. *Example:* an industrial welding or painting robot on a car assembly line; a robotic vacuum cleaner; a bomb-disposal robot.

questions.enonce_markdown: Discuss TWO factors that determine the reliability of an Information system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A reliable information system is one that gives accurate, complete and consistent information whenever it is needed. Two factors (1 mark each for the factor and its discussion; other valid factors are accepted):

1. **Quality and accuracy of the input data.** An information system can only be as good as the data fed into it (garbage in, garbage out). If data is entered wrongly, is incomplete or out of date, the information produced will be wrong and users will lose trust in it. Reliability is therefore improved by validation and verification of the input, and by trained data-entry staff.

2. **Quality, maintenance and fault tolerance of the hardware and software.** Hardware that fails often, software with bugs, or a system that is down because of power cuts or a lack of maintenance makes information unavailable. Reliability is improved by good-quality equipment, regular maintenance and updates, back-up power (UPS, generator), duplicated components (redundancy) and regular back-ups of the data.

Other possible factors: security against hackers and viruses, the training of users, the design and testing of the system before use.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify TWO natural hazards that can affect a computer system and give a measure that can be used to secure the data in each case. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Natural hazard | How it affects the computer system | Measure to secure the data |
|---|---|---|
| **Flood** (heavy rain, river overflow or water leakage) | Water short-circuits the equipment and destroys disks and cables; data is lost. | Keep servers and back-up media on upper floors or on raised platforms, never in a basement; keep **off-site back-ups** (or cloud back-ups) so that data can be restored on other machines. |
| **Fire** (often caused by lightning) | Heat and smoke destroy hardware, storage media and documents. | Install smoke detectors and gas or CO$_2$ fire extinguishers; store back-ups in a **fireproof safe** and in another building. |
| **Lightning / electrical storm** | A power surge burns the power supplies and the hard disks. | Use **surge protectors and UPS units**, lightning arresters on the building, and unplug equipment during storms. |
| **Extreme heat and humidity** | Overheating causes crashes and shortens the life of components; humidity causes corrosion. | Air-conditioned server room with humidity control, and regular back-ups. |

*Any TWO hazards with an appropriate measure each (1 mark for the hazard, 1 mark for the measure): 4 marks.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Distinguish between Simulation and Prototyping? (2 marks)

(b) List the steps used in prototyping. (2 marks)

(c) Give the role of end users' feedback in prototyping. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Simulation and prototyping (2 marks).**

- **Simulation** is the use of a computer model (mathematical or graphical) that imitates the behaviour of a real system or process, so that it can be studied, tested or predicted without the cost and danger of using the real thing. The model is not the final product. *Example:* a flight simulator used to train pilots, or a simulation of traffic flow before building a roundabout.
- **Prototyping** is the building of an early working (but incomplete) version of the real information system or software, which is shown to users, tested, and improved again and again until it becomes (or leads to) the final system. *Example:* a first version of a school management application with only the screens for registering students.

In short: a simulation *imitates how a real system would behave*; a prototype *is the first working version of the system that is going to be built*.

**(b) Steps used in prototyping (2 marks).**

1. Identify the basic requirements of the users (inputs, outputs, main functions).
2. Develop a working initial prototype (a quick, simplified version).
3. Users evaluate (test and review) the prototype and give their comments.
4. Revise and refine the prototype using the comments; steps 3 and 4 are repeated until users are satisfied.
5. The accepted prototype is completed, or used as the specification for the final system, which is then implemented.

**(c) Role of end users' feedback (1 mark).** End users' feedback shows what is wrong, missing or hard to use in the prototype, so that the developers can correct it and refine the requirements; the final system then really meets the users' needs and is more readily accepted by them.
